Friday: S&P 500 -3.70% to 6,910.39, Nasdaq Composite -5.28% to 22,617.73; week -8.61% and -10.02% (TradingKey)

top.headline: Pochettino starts with 4-0 defeat at Liverpool; United 19th after Yoro's 8th-minute red
top.why: The first read on the new manager is grim: one win in 11 league games and a leaky defence leave United one point above the bottom, with relegation talk starting. Pochettino disputes the red card and United are reportedly appealing.
points: Sun 22 Nov: Leny Yoro sent off in the 8th minute for DOGSO on Isak; VAR upheld it. Szoboszlai scored the free kick, then Wirtz (13'), Ngumoha (66') and Muñoz (82') made it 4-0.
United are 19th, one point above Crystal Palace, with one league win from 11. They have conceded 34 goals in all competitions, the most in Europe's top five leagues.
Pochettino and Fernandes both argue Isak lacked control of the ball so it should not have been a red; the Athletic headline says United will appeal (paywalled, not read).
Yoro faces a one-match ban, missing the trip to Brentford next weekend (SI).
top.next: Champions League at Sporting on 25 Nov; Brentford away next weekend (Yoro suspended); January defender search.

top.headline: Nvidia faces US questions on China chip sales as Huang exit clouds China business
top.why: Regulatory and leadership risk is now driving the AI sell-off as much as earnings.
points: Treasury Secretary Bessent said on 22 Nov the US wants answers on Nvidia's chip sales to China (Reuters)
Reuters says Huang's exit threatens Nvidia's China turnaround
US media reports cited by AFP say securities regulators are examining Nvidia's accounting; SEC has not named issues and no wrongdoing is established (Yahoo/BeInCrypto)
Nvidia's guidance of about $130bn next quarter assumes no China data-centre sales (TradingView)
top.next: No dated catalyst found; watch Nvidia CEO succession and chip export rules.

SI says Vusković, Bastoni, Murillo and Branthwaite are likely too costly; cheaper options and loans may be needed.
Linking United to these players is press speculation, not confirmed interest.
stories.next: January transfer window; Fulham contract outcome.

stories.headline: Anthropic stock gave back first-day gains by Friday as AI sell-off hit; filing shows heavy losses
stories.why: The first frontier-lab listing is now a live read on AI sentiment, and the S-1 figures show growth is being paid for with very large compute commitments.
points: IPO priced at $83 (980m shares, about $81.3bn raised, a record, plus $26bn private placement); opened 19 Nov at $111.50, closed day one at $97.17.
On Friday it fell to $83.05 intraday, five cents above the offer, and closed at $88.30 (CIO Africa) in a wider AI and chip sell-off; Nvidia and Broadcom each fell about 12%.
Filing figures reported by Reuters/Fortune: $16.3bn H1 2026 revenue, about 80% enterprise; $104bn nine-month net loss; nearly $900bn of compute commitments.
Fully diluted valuation near $1.75tn at the day-one close; about $1.5tn on outstanding shares.
stories.next: First quarterly report as a public company; date not seen in sources. Monday's 6:30 AM PT open is the next test of the AI trade.

stories.headline: AWS Quick adds Meta ads connector: create and edit campaigns by natural language
stories.why: Meta's ads MCP server is now reachable from third-party AI workspaces, so small teams can automate reporting and campaign edits without Ads Manager. It also widens what an AI agent with account access can change.
points: Connector gives AWS Quick access to Meta's ads MCP server operations, announced on AWS's blog.
Supports pulling performance insights, creating product catalogs and editing or creating campaigns, with dashboards and decks built from Meta plus first- and third-party data.
Setup is via Customize > Connectors with Facebook sign-in, choosing which Pages, Businesses and Instagram accounts Quick can access.
stories.next: No date; watch for Meta-side controls on agent edits and spend.

stories.headline: Bing puts ads in AI Overviews worldwide (ex-China); Google extends AI Mode ads
stories.why: Paid search is moving into AI answers on both major engines just before peak holiday spend, with little reporting to prove it pays. Check Microsoft Ads placement reports and keep Performance Max and AI Max in mind.
points: Microsoft announced ads in Bing AI Overviews on 19 Nov; they run through existing search campaigns with no new setup.
No placement-level controls or separate reporting announced; Microsoft's 21% purchase uplift figure is a Dec 2024 Copilot number, not for this placement.
Google has launched multiturn AI Mode ads in the US and expanded to 10 more English-language markets, naming three more for Q4 2026, with no pricing or performance data.
stories.next: Google's three further AI Mode ad markets in Q4 2026; no specific date given.

stories.headline: Bombay High Court refuses to restore Meta ad accounts of agency selling 'ban-proof' ads
stories.why: A court has backed Meta's right to cut off agencies that promise policy workarounds. If you buy through resellers or rented accounts, your campaigns can vanish with theirs.
points: 20 Nov order: Blink Digital India's four Business Managers (about 9,000 ad accounts) stay disabled before trial.
Court cited marketing of 'ban proof' ads, 'zero spend limits' and rented accounts, and 25 policy-violating ads Meta put on record.
Blink may ask Meta afresh to restore accounts if it commits to the rules; Meta must decide within two weeks. Its Rs 1,000-crore damages claim continues.
stories.next: Meta's decision within two weeks of any fresh request; trial date not reported.

stories.headline: US Catholic bishops' AI taskforce plans a nationwide lobbying push for AI regulation
stories.why: Global Christianity is moving from commentary on AI to organised political pressure, building on Pope Leo's encyclical. It is a marker of where church influence on AI policy may come from.
points: Bishop Oscar Cantú of San Jose, who leads the US bishops' AI taskforce, wants church leaders and congregations to build a 'groundswell' for regulation.
He presented at the bishops' plenary assembly last week; the taskforce has 8 clergy and 3 academic consultants and has been meeting AI developers.
He cited Pope Leo's encyclical Magnifica Humanitas, which says AI must be 'disarmed' and serve the common good.
He called for developer accountability for harm and more protection for children and vulnerable people.
stories.next: No dated event given; watch for specific bills or campaign materials from the bishops' conference.

stories.headline: Year-long JAMA trial: NAD supplement nicotinamide riboside does not help early Parkinson's
stories.why: NR is sold over the counter as a longevity and neuroprotection supplement. The largest trial yet found no benefit and slightly worse scores, so the earlier small-trial hope is not supported.
points: NOPARK, phase 3 RCT in Norway: 410 adults with early Parkinson's (mean age 65.6, 34% women), 500 mg NR twice daily vs placebo for 52 weeks.
MDS-UPDRS rose 2.45 points on NR vs a 0.27-point improvement on placebo (difference 2.72); statistically significant but below the clinically meaningful threshold.
No benefit on dopamine transporter scans or motor measures; nonmotor symptom scores were significantly worse on NR.
Blood NAD levels did rise, so the supplement was absorbed and adherence was about 99%.
stories.next: No dated catalyst; watch for commentary and any NR trials in other conditions.
stories.study: Single phase 3 double-blind RCT, n=410, early Parkinson's on levodopa-based treatment, one year, 500 mg twice daily only; extrapolating to healthy people or other doses is not supported. Read from News-Medical's write-up, not the JAMA paper.

stories.headline: Oxford commentary backs exercise for depression, citing updated Cochrane review of 73 trials
stories.why: Evidence that exercise performs about as well as therapy or antidepressants for depression, which suits a fitness-minded reader, though long-term data are thin.
points: Updated Cochrane review: 73 RCTs, at least 4,985 adults with depression; exercise moderately reduced symptoms vs no treatment or control.
Effects looked similar to psychological therapies and to antidepressant medication.
Group exercise is already recommended in NICE guidance; commentary published in BJPsych Advances.
Gaps: few studies on sustained benefit, and little on equity of access.
stories.study: Commentary on a Cochrane systematic review and meta-analysis of 73 RCTs (n of at least 4,985, adults with depression); limitations are short follow-up and variable trial quality, per the Oxford authors. Figures come from the Oxford Health press release.

stories.headline: Rockstar pushes first GTA VI patch, 01.002.002, with no patch notes yet
stories.why: This is the first post-launch fix after reports of PS5 crashes and save problems. Whether it fixes them is unknown until Rockstar publishes notes.
points: Version 01.002.002 went out Mon 23 Nov: 603.8MB on PS5, 1.6GB on Xbox Series X|S.
Rolled out in waves; ScreenRant citing dataminer Tex2 said about 33% of PS5 owners had it first.
No official patch notes at time of the reports; Insider Gaming calls crash/save fixes speculation.
Metacritic critic score is 99, user score 5.6 (ScreenRant), with review-bombing noted.
stories.next: Rockstar patch notes; PC port timing remains unconfirmed.

stories.headline: Hacker 'Cyberleek' claims a 209GB Xbox GTA VI build, threatens executable drop on 23 Nov
stories.why: Piracy and emulation risk could undercut the PC window and Rockstar's control of launch. It is a claim from an anonymous leaker with a crypto token to promote, so treat it sceptically.
points: Cyberleek says it holds the full November 2026 build and is distributing it by torrent.
Mashable says the files lack the executable, so the game isn't playable; Reddit users posted what they say are assets.
Cyberleek threatens to release the executable on 23 Nov, or sooner if its token hits a $15M market cap, and claims emulation within a week.
Not independently verified; no Rockstar or Take-Two response seen.
stories.next: Cyberleek's own 23 Nov deadline; any Take-Two response.

stories.headline: Aeon: an environmental historian argues El Niño is as much a human construct as a natural event
stories.why: With the 2026-27 El Niño possibly the strongest in 1,000 years, this essay shows why it is hard to forecast and how past events killed millions yet enriched others. Worth reading for the history of a force that will shape coming weather.
points: The author says 2026 Pacific warming may be the strongest El Niño in 1,000 years; impacts are still uncertain.
'El Niño' began as a Peruvian fishermen's name for a December warm current; Camilo Carrillo introduced it to science in 1892.
It is now understood as the ocean side of the Southern Oscillation pressure seesaw; its worldwide teleconnections are less consistent than usually presented.
An opinion essay by a historian, not a forecast; the 'strongest in 1,000 years' line is the author's, not a source-checked finding.
stories.next: No dated catalyst; read the 26-minute essay.

updates.headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO; Nvidia up about a third, Nasdaq nearly 7%
updates.why: The board reversed itself 11 days after Huang resigned, which overturns the 'Huang exit' premise in this morning's third lead. It set off the biggest AI-complex rebound of the sell-off, clawing back more than half of last week's plunge.
points: Nvidia's board reinstated Huang as CEO, effective immediately, days after rejecting his offer to return (AP, Reuters, 23 Nov)
Nvidia shares surged about 28–33% and the Nasdaq rose nearly 7%; Reuters says the rally could add about $2tn to the Nasdaq-100
Trump says he urged the board and that Huang posed no national security threat; Democrats and some Republicans are criticising the move
The Senate Banking Committee has set Huang's testimony for 3 Dec (The Hill)
updates.next: PCE inflation report Wed 25 Nov; Huang's Senate Banking testimony 3 Dec
